# Growth Log Pattern Extraction

Curated by Skill Harbor: a methodology that fixes the most common learning-log failure, writing "fixed a bug in X" and calling it growth. A real growth log extracts the pattern so you recognize it next time. Three rules govern every entry. Rule 1, failures beat achievements: one two-hour bug teaches more than three features that worked first try, so write the pattern (session cookie SameSite defaulting to Lax in Chrome 128+, pattern: always set SameSite=None; Secure explicitly) not the event. Rule 2, the Bole Principle: before writing, search existing entries for the same root cause; same root cause with different symptoms gets merged, never duplicated. Rule 3, every entry must be transferable: if you cannot write "next time I see [signal], I will [action]", you have not extracted the pattern yet. The template runs 4-8 sentences across Context, Root Cause, The Pattern, and Related sections, with four entry types (Failure, Methodology, Pattern Discovery, Capability Change) and a quality checklist covering title discipline, the transferable sentence, signal specificity, and duplicate search. It pairs with the delivery-gate Stop hook: the hook enforces that a learning file was touched today, this skill ensures the content inside is worth keeping. Works with any note system: Markdown files, Notion, Obsidian, plain text. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: only log when a pattern emerges (debugging, redo...
